posts:
When state security forces turn to chemical terror, the mask of public protection melts away.

Jakarta Acid Attack Sentencing
Evidence: national defense, state-sponsored terror, rule of law
#HumanRights #Indonesia

Military intelligence officers claim to operate in the interest of national security and public order, protecting the state from subversion.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, +1.0) — Greater Good

Officers used sulphuric acid to permanently disfigure a human rights activist, executing an act of pure terror and violent extraction.
Resulting Judgement: (-2.0, -2.0) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
State actors tasked with protection instead used maximum destructive force to silence dissent, exposing a complete inversion of their mandate.
Four Indonesian military intelligence officers have been sentenced to up to three years in prison for a brutal acid attack on a human rights activist in Jakarta.

The Bright Side:
The sentencing of these officers represents a crucial, albeit brief, moment of judicial accountability against state-sponsored violence.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The state frames this as rogue behavior (WHAT). Structurally, it is a failure of systemic Will (WHO) where state power is weaponized.

It is a bait-and-switch: security forces extracting safety from citizens.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between national defense and state-sponsored chemical violence...
...it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil. When state power is used to actively destroy citizens, the system collapses into pure tyranny.

The Unavoidable Truth: A state that tolerates violence from its security forces is a threat to its own people.

The Unavoidable Lie: That attacking activists protects national security.

Alethekanon:
This is a catastrophic systemic failure. When intelligence officers weaponize chemical violence against citizens, the state's monopoly on force has degenerated into raw terror.

Awwthekanon:
It is heartbreaking to think of the pain and fear this activist endured. True security should protect those who speak up for the vulnerable, not scar them.

Brothekanon:
Imagine being in military intelligence and thinking throwing acid on an activist makes you a hero. Glad they got jail time, but three years seems way too light for that.
